findings.title: Decoration-persistence ownership is still undefined at the architecture seam after the SPEC-07 C1 change
findings.location: SPEC-00 §1 Module Map; SPEC-00 §2 Seam E and Seam H; SPEC-07 v1.1.2 changelog C1 / SDR-07-012
findings.evidence: SPEC-00 Module Map lists `SPEC-05 ... Depends On | SPEC-01, SPEC-03, SPEC-07`; Seam E says `SPEC-05 has no direct assembly reference to SPEC-04`; Seam H says `The vocabulary layer emits decoration payloads ... SPEC-04's DhfDecorationWriter persists`; SPEC-07 C1 says `SPEC-05 persists the payload via SPEC-04's DhfDecorationWriter after AppendTurnAsync returns entry_id`.
findings.problem: The orchestration contract still describes the old persistence path while SPEC-07 moved persistence responsibility to SPEC-05. There is no authoritative SPEC-05→SPEC-04 seam, dependency declaration, or interface contract for the post-AppendTurnAsync decoration write path.
findings.why_it_matters: This will break implementation planning, architecture tests, and project references first: one spec forbids a SPEC-05→SPEC-04 dependency while another requires it.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an explicit seam and module dependency for SPEC-05→SPEC-04 decoration persistence, name the exact interface(s) SPEC-05 consumes, and remove stale text implying SPEC-07 persists directly.

findings.title: `GetFeatureTreeInput` still lacks the `Compressed` wire field required by the add-in service contract
findings.evidence: SPEC-01 defines `public record GetFeatureTreeInput : IToolInput { public bool IncludeSuppressed { get; init; } = false; }` while SPEC-02 defines `IReadOnlyList<FeatureNode> GetFeatureTree(bool includeSuppressed, bool compressed);`.
findings.problem: The cross-process DTO cannot express whether the caller wants compressed or full feature-tree output, but the add-in-side service requires that parameter.
findings.why_it_matters: The orchestrator and add-in cannot implement or test the same contract. Either the viewer/agent cannot request full output, or the add-in must invent a default not specified on the wire.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `Compressed` to `GetFeatureTreeInput` with default and semantics in SPEC-01, or remove the `compressed` service parameter and document a fixed behavior everywhere.

findings.title: SPEC-02 still uses an unsupported `FeatureTreeHash = "OVERSIZE"` fallback
findings.evidence: `The resulting ToolResultMessage substitutes a placeholder StateAfter (feature tree empty, IsFeatureTreeTruncated = true, FeatureTreeHash = "OVERSIZE") ...`
findings.problem: `OVERSIZE` is not a valid `FeatureTreeHash` value under SPEC-01, which only defines a real hash or the `NO_DOCUMENT` sentinel for null-document state.
findings.why_it_matters: This creates protocol-invalid state snapshots that will fail validation and hash-based change detection, and it encourages consumers to special-case an undocumented sentinel.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the placeholder with a SPEC-01-compliant snapshot: keep a real hash of the complete tree, or define a new protocol-level sentinel in SPEC-01 and update validators/tests accordingly.

findings.title: Planned-disconnect escalation still contradicts the teardown send path
findings.evidence: §9.0.2 sends teardown directly with `_webSocket.SendAsync(...)`; §9.1.1 step 3 says `Do NOT attempt to send AddinTeardownMessage. The send path goes through SwUiThreadCommandQueue and would block behind the stuck COM call.`
findings.problem: The spec simultaneously says teardown send is direct WebSocket I/O and that it is blocked behind the SolidWorks UI-thread queue.
findings.why_it_matters: Shutdown behavior, observability (`explicit_shutdown` vs `heartbeat_timeout`), and test expectations cannot be implemented consistently.
findings.proposed_fix: Pick one authoritative threading model for teardown send and update both the normal and escalation paths, including closure-reason expectations and tests.

findings.title: Day-0 validation still checks a nonexistent DHF closure-reason field
findings.evidence: `confirm the orchestrator's DHF session row shows closure reason explicit_shutdown`
findings.problem: The current cross-spec contract says closure reason is not stored in `dhf.sessions`; it is only emitted in structured logs.
findings.why_it_matters: This acceptance check is unexecutable as written and invites an implementer to add out-of-spec schema just to satisfy the test.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the validation step to inspect the structured log event (`session_closed`) or another explicitly specified observability surface, not the DHF row.

findings.title: SPEC-07 still claims pipeline success waits for durable DHF persistence after that responsibility moved to SPEC-05
findings.evidence: §0 says `The pipeline returns success ONLY after the citation is durably written`; SDR-07-006 says `The write is awaited on the critical path ... pipeline success is reported only after durable persistence.`
findings.problem: Those statements are incompatible with SPEC-07 v1.1.2 C1, which moved persistence to SPEC-05 after `AppendTurnAsync` returns `entry_id`.
findings.why_it_matters: Callers cannot know whether a SPEC-07 success means 'payload assembled' or 'decoration durably stored', which breaks retry, telemetry, and acceptance criteria.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite SPEC-07 success semantics so a successful SPEC-07 result means payload assembly only, and move durable-write guarantees entirely into the SPEC-05 contract.

findings.title: `StageLatencies` still requires `DecorationWriteMs` and `TotalMs` even though SPEC-07 no longer performs the write
findings.evidence: `StageLatencies` includes `DecorationWriteMs` and `TotalMs`, while §3.2 says `decoration INSERT is SPEC-05's budget` and Stage 5 is `In-memory DTO construction; no I/O`.
findings.problem: SPEC-07's output model requires latency fields that SPEC-07 cannot compute before returning `PipelineResult`.
findings.why_it_matters: Implementers must either fabricate values, mutate the returned object in SPEC-05, or violate the documented ownership boundary.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove `DecorationWriteMs` and `TotalMs` from SPEC-07's `StageLatencies`, or define a separate SPEC-05-owned envelope that augments the pipeline result after persistence.

findings.title: The viewer's raw-input privacy gate has no tenant-scoped configuration contract
findings.evidence: SDR-06-008 says the gate is `provisioned per-tenant ... as a tenant-level configuration flag (ViewerOptions.VocabRawInputAllowed)`, but §3 defines `ViewerOptions` with only `EnableStretchEndpoints`, and §13 shows no `vocabRawInputAllowed` or tenant-keyed settings.
findings.problem: The spec promises per-tenant gating for raw utterance/parsed-intent display, but provides no config schema or lookup interface to vary that behavior by tenant.
findings.why_it_matters: The privacy control cannot be implemented as specified; the likely fallback is a global flag, which would overexpose or overhide data across tenants.
findings.proposed_fix: Define a tenant-keyed configuration source or resolver interface for `vocab_view_raw_input`, and add the concrete config shape used by SPEC-06 at runtime.

top_3_must_fix: Add an explicit SPEC-05→SPEC-04 decoration-persistence seam/dependency and remove stale direct SPEC-07 persistence language.
Reconcile `GetFeatureTreeInput` with the add-in service by adding/removing the `Compressed` parameter consistently.
Remove the invalid `FeatureTreeHash = "OVERSIZE"` fallback and make oversize snapshots conform to SPEC-01.
